question.problem:
Jennifer is doing a science experiment in her Chemistry class. She takes a liquid with a temperature of ${10.1}^{∘}\text{C}$ and places it in a refrigerator. After half an hour, she removes the liquid from the refrigerator and places it on a table. She concludes that the temperature decreased by ${12.7}^{∘}\text{C}.$

After half an hour, Jennifer takes the temperature of the liquid again and finds that the temperature increased by ${8}^{∘}\text{C}.$ What is the final temperature of the liquid?
question.worked_solution:
First of all, we must determine the temperature of the liquid when it was removed from the refrigerator. Since its temperature decreased by ${12.7}^{∘}\text{C}$ compared to the initial temperature, we must subtract the variation in temperature from the initial temperature. This gives

$$
{10.1}^{∘}\text{C}-{12.7}^{∘}\text{C}=-{2.6}^{∘}\text{C}.
$$

Now, we must determine the temperature of the liquid after half an hour had elapsed. Since the temperature of the liquid increased by ${8}^{∘}\text{C}$ compared to the temperature when it was removed from the refrigerator, we add the variation in temperature to the temperature of the liquid when it was removed from the refrigerator. This gives

$$
-{2.6}^{∘}\text{C}+{8}^{∘}\text{C}={5.4}^{∘}\text{C}.
$$

Therefore, the final temperature of the liquid is ${5.4}^{∘}\text{C}.$
